title: Structs: Giving a Group of Numbers One Name

questions.question: Why group x, y and theta into a struct instead of passing three numbers?
options: C++ functions cannot take more than two arguments
Because doubles cannot be passed individually
They travel as one value with named parts, so they cannot be reordered by accident
Structs make the program run faster
questions.explanation: Loose numbers in the same order are easy to swap and the compiler cannot help. A named type makes the group one thing with labelled parts.

questions.question: What does writing = 0.0 after a struct member achieve?
options: Nothing, it is only a comment for readers
Every new instance starts at a known value instead of leftover memory
It makes the member read only
It reserves memory for the member
questions.explanation: A default member initialiser means the type is born valid. Without it, reading an uninitialised member is undefined behaviour.

questions.question: Why does distance ignore theta?
options: Because theta is always zero in practice
Because mixing angles and metres would overflow
Two robots on the same spot facing opposite ways are still zero metres apart
Because std::hypot only accepts two arguments
questions.explanation: Distance is about position. Heading is a separate question, and mixing the two into one number would produce something with no physical meaning.

questions.question: Why does the reference use std::hypot instead of sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)?
options: It is the only way to compute a square root in C++
It gives the same answer without overflowing on very large differences
It automatically ignores the heading
It is required when the arguments are doubles
questions.explanation: Squaring a very large difference can overflow before the square root is taken. hypot computes the same value while avoiding that.

questions.question: Why does midpoint set theta to zero rather than averaging the two headings?
options: Because the tests do not check theta
Because averaging two doubles is undefined
Because zero is the most common heading
Averaging angles is wrong when they wrap, so the function does not claim to do it
questions.explanation: The average of 179 degrees and minus 179 degrees is zero, which points the opposite way from both. Refusing to answer is better than answering wrongly.

questions.question: What does the ROS 2 Pose message add compared with this struct?
options: A three dimensional position and an orientation held as a quaternion
Automatic unit conversion between metres and feet
Nothing, it is exactly the same
A built in distance function
questions.explanation: ROS poses describe three dimensions, so orientation needs more than one angle. Phase 06 explains why a quaternion is used for that.
